body:
I am not sure a lot can be done here considering that polygon outline ops are inherently picky when it comes to certain input.

The agent radius can't be really disabled while the input layout includes a mix to form the perfect mortal sin that can be done for polygon outline calculations (integer snapped vertices + axis aligned edges + nested outlines + corner vertex overlap).

> This issue doesn't happen if navigation_region.navigation_polygon.agent_radius is above 0.

There is the solution.

The reason why the agent radius is a solution is because due to its (tiny) offset it fixes all the rasterization and interpretation issues caused by the bad input as it reinterprets all the outlines after the offset. Without agent radius the raw input is consumed and the result, while not technically wrong, is interpreted wrong causing flipped polygons which is unwanted.

The baking rect also does a quick cutout that does not reinterpret all the outlines again, which means if there are already some nested outline interpretation errors they get amplified by using the baking rect. The agent radius before basically fixes the errors so the baking rect can work reliable. I am not sure why this combo is even used considering that the baking rect is designed for chunk baking with agent radius. Without an agent radius it is not really needed. Just an outline with this rect shape can be added instead that does the same simpler and more reliable.
